walkthroughs.body_html:
Business Activity, Marketing and People — a core area of GCSE Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Business Activity, Marketing and People brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Business Activity, Marketing and People.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does the 'S' in SMART objectives stand for?
options: Strategic
Specific
Strong
Saleable

mcqs.q: Which 1970 essay argued the 'social responsibility of business is to increase profits'?
options: Drucker
Porter
Friedman
Carroll

mcqs.q: What are the four Ps of the marketing mix?
options: The four Ps are Product, Price, Profit, and People.
Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion — the controllable variables a business uses to satisfy customers and achieve objectives.
A brand is the company that makes a product.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.

mcqs.q: What is a brand in marketing?
options: A combination of name, design, symbols and associations that distinguishes a product and creates customer perception and loyalty — more than just a logo.
A brand is the company that makes a product.
A brand is just the logo on a product.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.

mcqs.q: Why are cash flow and profit different on different time-scales?
options: Profit is recognised when a sale is made (even on credit); cash flow is when money actually moves. A profitable sale today may produce no cash for 60 days while bills are due — creating a cash-flow problem despite profit.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.
A brand is the company that makes a product.
Cash flow and profit are the same thing measured differently.
